title: Katie Zacharia is out as White House press secretary a week after Trump named her
dek: She gave one briefing. Outlets differ on whether she was fired or is moving to another role.
what: President Trump announced on Friday 9 October that Katie Zacharia would be White House press secretary, CBS News reported then. She was a conservative commentator and senior communications adviser at Trump Media, and had spent about six weeks as a Department of Homeland Security spokesperson earlier in 2026, according to Fox News.
She gave her first and only briefing on Tuesday 13 October. CBS reports she took questions from three outlets and the session was short. Fox News puts it at 14 minutes.

On Friday 16 October, Trump told reporters on the South Lawn that she did not have to do the job and that he thought she should reconsider, CBS and Fox report. Asked whether he was firing her, he said no, Fox reports.

The reports then differ on her status. CBS News reports, citing two US officials, that she was removed after five days, and says the New York Times first reported she had been fired. Fox News quotes a senior White House official saying she is "transitioning out". CBS says she was expected to move to a new administration role. No replacement had been announced when CBS wrote.

Outlets also reported a dispute over how she described her legal training. CBS reports she presented herself as a lawyer although she failed the California bar exam in 2011, and that she acknowledged that on Thursday. CBS quotes her as saying she never came across as someone who was an attorney at law.

CNN's Kaitlan Collins posted that she was told Trump was embarrassed by the coverage and that aides did not defend Zacharia. Collins also says Trump decided she had to go after a Fox News interview with Sean Hannity. That account rests on Collins' unnamed sources and I could not confirm it elsewhere.
why: The press secretary is the White House's public voice, and the job is open again after standing empty from August to October. Clips from her Hannity interview and jokes about her short tenure carried the story.

worlds.name: Reports that she was fired
worlds.sees: Two officials told CBS she was removed after five days, and the New York Times reported a firing.

worlds.name: The White House account
worlds.sees: A senior official says she is transitioning out, and Trump says he is not firing her and wants to spare her the media treatment.

common: Established by CBS and Fox: Zacharia was named on 9 October, briefed once on 13 October, and by 16 October was leaving the press secretary job, with Trump saying she should reconsider. Not established: whether she was fired or chose to go. The two accounts above use different words for the same exit, and the sources on each side are unnamed officials. The reason Collins gives for the decision rests on her sources alone.
next: A named announcement of her next role, and of a new press secretary.

corrections.text: The story was written when she was named. It now covers her exit on 16 October, and its standing changed from established to developing.
